about.en: A defended shoulder throw invites your partner to press into your back; sliding a leg behind their heels and dropping to the side takes them backwards into the valley.

en: Take your right grips and turn in for Ippon-seoi-nage, your right arm under their right armpit.
Feel them stop the throw by pressing their chest and their weight forward into your back.
Stop asking for the lift. Keep the sleeve and turn your chest so you face the same way as them, your hip against theirs.
Extend your right leg low and straight behind both of their legs, sitting your hip down towards the mat.
Sit down close beside them and drive your shoulders back over your extended leg.
They fall backwards over your leg onto their side; keep the sleeve so their head does not follow their hips down.

receiving.en: Leaning into their back is a common way to kill a shoulder throw, and it hands them this one: your weight is already behind your heels when their leg slides in behind both of your legs. You go backwards over a barrier you cannot step over, with them dropping beside you. Do not put a hand out behind you. Chin on your chest, slap with your free arm, and let the held sleeve turn you slightly onto your side as you land.

viNotes.en: Their forward pressure on your back is unmistakable, and it is the cue to stop lifting and change direction. Keep the sleeve throughout: it is what tells you where their body is once you turn to face the same way, and it is what keeps their head off the mat at the finish. You both end up on the mat, so agree the direction of work and know where the edge is.

cue.en: The blocked shoulder throw becomes a sit-down drop: a leg slides behind their heels and both go back.
